independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.95.1-Ps.95.2 and its closing seam verify. Ps 95 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json: rule identity, web_title false), so web:Ps.95.1 = oshb:Ps.95.1 and no dual-cite arithmetic is at issue; the offset map records web_title false, so 0 of this psalm's 11 WEB verses is a title pseudo-ref and the row correctly opens on verse text. Both quoted runs collate at byte tier: לְ֭כוּ נְרַנְּנָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.95.1) and נְקַדְּמָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.95.2). Both 2 of 2 WEB quotes are verbatim: “Oh come, let’s sing to Yahweh.” (web:Ps.95.1) and “Let’s come before his presence with thanksgiving.” (web:Ps.95.2). The seam driver is tier-1 and holds: כִּ֤י (oshb:Ps.95.3) opens the grounds clause that web:Ps.95.3 renders “For Yahweh is a great God”, and a skeleton sweep of that particle across MT 95:4-95:5 returns 0 of 2 verses, so nothing competes with the 95:2|95:3 cut inside the following unit. Confidence high is calibrated. Observation, not filed as a challenge: the rationale calls נְקַדְּמָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.95.2) 'the same imperative-plural voice' while glossing it 'let us come before', a first-person plural volitive rather than a plural imperative; the row's own signal field states the alternative correctly as 'imperative or cohortative-plural forms', so the looseness is self-corrected inside the row. The one defect is register.

challenges.claim: device_notes carries a positional row reference, which the standing register purge bans in row prose.
challenges.evidence: The field reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'Every row below answers to the same parent, Psalm 95.' 'Row below' is a file-order/positional reference to other rows; the standing rule is that cross-row references are verse-anchored, never positional or id-anchored. The same mandated parent-grouping sentence is discharged without any positional word in this cluster's Ps 96 and Ps 97 opening rows ('its rows group under one parent'; 'All rows of this psalm belong to a single parent unit'), so 2 of the 3 attested variation-order formulations here are already clean and the cure is a one-sentence swap. No text claim is affected: parent_psalm 95 is correct for all 4 rows spanning Ps.95.1-Ps.95.11.

reviews.reasoning: The span Ps.95.3-Ps.95.5 and both its seams verify. כִּ֤י אֵ֣ל גָּד֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.95.3) collates at byte tier and is the causal opener; MT 95:4 and MT 95:5 both open אֲשֶׁ֣ר (oshb:Ps.95.4) / אֲשֶׁר (oshb:Ps.95.5), relative particles subordinate to 95:3, so the grounds unit is genuinely 3 verses; MT 95:6 opens בֹּ֭אוּ (oshb:Ps.95.6), a fresh volitive summons, so the closing seam at 95:5|95:6 is tier-1. I re-derived the row's absence claim and it is TRUE: a skeleton sweep of the causal particle over MT 95:4-95:5 returns 0 of 2 verses. The claim is nevertheless stated without the mandated digit-bearing sweep and check_universals.py flags it (path observed_substrate_signals[0], claim 'with no further -clause before web:Ps'); since the underlying fact holds I record that as an observation rather than a separate challenge. Two defects are filed: an unmirrored out-of-span verse appeal, and a misdescription of 95:5.

challenges.claim: rejected_alternative argues from verses outside the row's span without mirroring them into boundary_evidence_refs.
challenges.evidence: The field reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'web:Ps.95.6 returns to the imperative register of vv.1-2 rather than continuing the causal, descriptive clauses of vv.3-5, so carrying this row through it was rejected.' The appeal to vv.1-2 resolves against the row's own span psalm to web:Ps.95.1 and web:Ps.95.2, both outside the span Ps.95.3-Ps.95.5; boundary_evidence_refs holds only 3 entries, web:Ps.95.3, web:Ps.95.5 and web:Ps.95.6, so neither appears. The warrant is sound on the merits (MT 95:1 opens לְ֭כוּ at oshb:Ps.95.1 and MT 95:6 opens בֹּ֭אוּ at oshb:Ps.95.6, both byte) - the defect is provenance, and the cure is adding the 2 refs. check_refs_mirror.py returns GREEN on this row only because its bare-verse arm requires whitespace after the abbreviation: on the delivered string 'vv.1-2' its VERSE_WORD pattern matches 0 spans, while on 'vv. 1-2' it matches 1.

challenges.claim: The rationale misdescribes web:Ps.95.5, attaching the hands to the sea and dropping the dry land.
challenges.evidence: The rationale reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'the sea Yahweh made with his own hands (web:Ps.95.5)'. The verse divides the two acts across its 2 cola: ל֣וֹ הַ֭יָּם וְה֣וּא עָשָׂ֑הוּ is predicated of the sea and וְ֝יַבֶּ֗שֶׁת יָדָ֥יו יָצָֽרוּ of the dry land (both byte, oshb:Ps.95.5). WEB agrees: “The sea is his, and he made it. His hands formed the dry land.” (web:Ps.95.5). The row's device_notes inventory of the span's creation imagery ('deep places, mountains, sea') likewise omits the dry land, so the same recut fixes both fields.

reviews.reasoning: The span Ps.95.6-Ps.95.7 holds and the 95:7|95:8 seam is correctly placed. בֹּ֭אוּ נִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֣ה (oshb:Ps.95.6) collates at byte tier and is a second volitive summons answering לְ֭כוּ (oshb:Ps.95.1); the row's speaker argument is right, since the first-person object suffixes that identify the oracle's speaker first appear at MT 95:9 in נִ֭סּוּנִי and בְּ֝חָנ֗וּנִי (both byte, oshb:Ps.95.9), 2 verses after the pivot, and nothing in MT 95:7 marks a speaker change. The 4 WEB quotes in the rationale are verbatim. Observation, not filed: this psalm's opening seam is driven by the causal particle at 95:2|95:3, and the same particle opens 95:7 inside this row (כִּ֘י ה֤וּא אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ, byte, oshb:Ps.95.7); a rival cut at 95:6|95:7 is therefore available on the row's own criterion and is not disclosed in rejected_alternative, which addresses the 95:7c edge instead. I do not judge that rival superior - a 95:6-only row would orphan the 7c pivot the row correctly identifies - so I file no challenge on the span, only on quotation fidelity.

challenges.claim: device_notes attributes to web:Ps.95.7 a rendering the WEB text does not carry, and the row renders other WEB material in straight quotes where the checker cannot see it.
challenges.evidence: device_notes reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'Today, if you would hear his voice,' attributed to web:Ps.95.7. WEB reads “Today, oh that you would hear his voice!” (web:Ps.95.7); ps_lib.web_quote_found returns False for the device_notes form and True for the WEB form against that verse's folded text. The row's own rationale carries the verbatim form, so the 2 fields disagree about the same clause. The 'if' rendering tracks MT הַ֝יּ֗וֹם אִֽם בְּקֹל֥וֹ תִשְׁמָֽעוּ (byte, oshb:Ps.95.7) rather than the English witness it is cited to. Same cure site: the rationale puts WEB material in straight quotes ('we are the people of his pasture', web:Ps.95.7, against WEB “We are the people of his pasture,”), which places it outside check_web_quotes.py's reach - the convention reserves curly quotes for WEB text precisely so the checker can see it.

reviews.reasoning: The span Ps.95.8-Ps.95.11 and the oracle warrant verify. All 5 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier: כִּמְרִיבָ֑ה and כְּי֥וֹם מַ֝סָּ֗ה (oshb:Ps.95.8), נִ֭סּוּנִי and בְּ֝חָנ֗וּנִי (oshb:Ps.95.9), אַרְבָּ֘עִ֤ים שָׁנָ֨ה (oshb:Ps.95.10). The rejected_alternative's syntactic argument is correct: MT 95:9 opens אֲשֶׁ֣ר (oshb:Ps.95.9), a relative particle binding it to the wilderness clause of 95:8, so the 2 verses are one sentence and the oracle cannot be opened at 95:9. The exclusivity claim in device_notes is TRUE as re-derived (see the count challenge for the digits), and the span runs to the psalm's last verse, MT 95:11 of 11. Two defects are filed. Observation, not filed: the glosses 'Meribah' and 'the day of Massah' do not cover the prefixed comparative in the quoted runs כִּמְרִיבָ֑ה and כְּי֥וֹם (oshb:Ps.95.8), which WEB renders “as at Meribah, as in the day of Massah” (web:Ps.95.8) - a quote/gloss parity trim, cheap to recut alongside the count repair.

challenges.claim: The signal's widened absence claim is contradicted by the inventory it cites: pmarks_Ps.json records a paseq seg inside the span.
challenges.evidence: The signal reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'no Selah or other disclosure-inventory mark falls within this span (pmarks_Ps.json)'. The selah half is right: 0 of the 71 selah verses fall in MT 95:8-95:11. The widened half is false - pmarks_Ps.json paseq holds Ps.95.10 with 1 seg, and Ps 95 is an identity psalm, so MT 95:10 is inside the span at web:Ps.95.10. The seg sits against the row's own quoted run: pmarks records 1 paseq in the verse whose opening אַרְבָּ֘עִ֤ים שָׁנָ֨ה (byte, oshb:Ps.95.10) the rationale quotes. I cite paseq here only as an inventory fact and offer it as no part of any boundary argument - it is seg-layer, single-witness, and not a driver. The cure is to scope the claim to selah, as the Ps 96 row in this cluster already does, or to disclose the paseq with its single-witness label.

challenges.claim: The exclusivity sweep blends two distinct names into one object and reports the window size instead of the swept object's hit count.
challenges.evidence: device_notes reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'The Meribah/Massah rebellion (web:Ps.95.8) is not named elsewhere across this part's 70 verses (sweep: 70 verses, Ps.91-95)'. Two distinct spellings are swept as one class, and the only digit given is the window (WEB Ps.91-95 does hold 70 numbered verses, re-derived). Per-object counts, unit named: skeleton sweep of the prefixed form כִּמְרִיבָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.95.8) = 1 verse book-wide, MT 95:8; skeleton sweep of the prefix-stripped name = 3 verses book-wide, MT 81:8, MT 95:8, MT 106:32, of which 1 lies in MT 91-95; skeleton sweep of מַ֝סָּ֗ה (oshb:Ps.95.8) = 2 verses book-wide, MT 6:7 and MT 95:8, where the MT 6:7 hit is a substring collision inside a different word and not the place name; WEB phrase sweeps give 3 verses for the one name and 1 verse for the other. The row's conclusion survives all 4 sweeps - only its count object and digit need recutting.

reviews.reasoning: The span Ps.96.1-Ps.96.6 and the 96:6|96:7 seam verify. Ps 96 is an identity psalm whose offset-map entry records web_title false, so 0 of its 13 WEB verses is a title pseudo-ref, the row correctly opens on verse text, and no dual-cite arithmetic is at issue. שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ (oshb:Ps.96.1) and הָב֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת עַמִּ֑ים (oshb:Ps.96.7) both collate at byte tier, and the vocative imperative cluster at MT 96:7 is a genuine tier-1 reopening of the address, so the seam sits where the row puts it. The causal reading of the interior also checks out: MT 96:4 and MT 96:5 both open with the same causal particle, 2 verses of grounds running into the sanctuary colon of MT 96:6. All 6 curly WEB quotes check verbatim. Both filed defects are in the cross-psalm new-song note. Observation, not filed separately: check_web_quotes.py flags observed_substrate_signals[0] as a curly quote with no web: ref in its field - the quoted words are WEB text of web:Ps.96.1 but the field carries only an oshb: ref, and the standing rule makes curly quotes plus an inline web: ref in the SAME field mandatory at every layer.

challenges.claim: The four-word sharing claim is carried by a three-word byte quote that is not the cited verse's opening, and the sharing holds only at skeleton tier, which the row does not name.
challenges.evidence: device_notes claims the clause 'shares its first four Hebrew words with the opening of web:Ps.98.1' and offers as byte evidence a run of 3 words, שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֨ה שִׁ֣יר (byte, oshb:Ps.98.1) - the fourth word is absent from the quote. That run is also not the opening of the cited MT verse: oshb:Ps.98.1 opens מִזְמ֡וֹר, the superscription word that WEB carries at the title pseudo-ref web:Ps.98.0 (offset map: Ps 98 identity, web_title true, mt_title_verses empty), so the WEB-side opening and the MT-side opening are not the same string and the equation needs that disclosure. The sharing itself is skeleton-tier only: a byte sweep of שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ (oshb:Ps.96.1) returns 1 verse book-wide, MT 96:1; the fourth words differ, חָדָ֑שׁ (oshb:Ps.96.1) against חָ֭דָשׁ (oshb:Ps.98.1); and an accent_stripped comparison of the two four-word runs is False, with only skeleton equal. Tier discipline requires the tier be named wherever the sharing is asserted, not only in the parenthetical count.

challenges.claim: The new-song sweep is mis-scoped to the row's span and its digit is wrong at book scope.
challenges.evidence: device_notes reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'skeleton sweep: 2 verses carry this exact four-word new-song clause within this span, 96:1 and 98:1'. The row's declared span is Ps.96.1-Ps.96.6, and 1 of the 2 named verses lies inside it - web:Ps.98.1 does not, so the scope word is false on the row's own face and the reader is given no other range against which to re-derive the digit. Re-derived book-wide with the object named first (the four-word clause שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ, oshb:Ps.96.1) and the unit named: skeleton sweep = 3 verses, MT 96:1, MT 98:1 and MT 149:1, all 3 identity psalms so the WEB refs carry the same numbers. MT 149:1 is unnamed by the row, so no scope makes the delivered pair both correct and complete: 1 verse inside the span, 3 verses book-wide.

reviews.reasoning: The span Ps.96.7-Ps.96.13 holds: the vocative cluster opens at MT 96:7 with הָב֣וּ (oshb:Ps.96.7), the unit runs to the psalm's last verse, MT 96:13 of 13, and both quoted runs collate at byte tier, including the full-verse run at oshb:Ps.96.13. The selah claim is correct and correctly scoped: 0 of the 71 selah verses fall in MT 96:7-96:13, and the row labels it span-scoped. Observation, not filed: the rationale says the register 'shifts from imperative to declarative at web:Ps.96.10', but MT 96:10 opens אִמְר֤וּ (byte, oshb:Ps.96.10), a plural imperative continuing the series הָב֣וּ (oshb:Ps.96.7), הָב֣וּ (oshb:Ps.96.8) and הִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ (oshb:Ps.96.9) - the declarative material is the embedded proclamation and the 2 cola after it, which the row's own rejected_alternative describes correctly, so the two fields disagree about where the register turns.

challenges.claim: The kingship-clause sweep is mis-scoped, leaves its tier unnamed, and its ordinal contradicts its own list.
challenges.evidence: The signal reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'one of two attested clause forms of this proclamation in this span (sweep: 3 verses, web:Ps.96.10, web:Ps.97.1, web:Ps.99.1; the third occurrence is at web:Ps.93.1, outside this span)'. Against the row's declared span Ps.96.7-Ps.96.13 only 1 of the 3 named verses lies inside, so the scope word is false as delivered, and no range is given against which the digit could be re-derived. Calling web:Ps.93.1 'the third occurrence' immediately after a list of 3 refs leaves the ordinal contradicting the count. Re-derived with the object named first (the clause יְהוָ֣ה מָ֭לָךְ, oshb:Ps.97.1) and the unit named: skeleton sweep = 6 verses book-wide, MT 10:16, MT 29:10, MT 93:1, MT 96:10, MT 97:1, MT 99:1; accent_stripped = 4 verses, MT 93:1, MT 96:10, MT 97:1, MT 99:1; byte = 2 verses, MT 97:1 and MT 99:1. The 2 extra skeleton hits are the short-token homograph the toolkit warns about - MT 10:16 מֶ֭לֶךְ (oshb:Ps.10.16) and MT 29:10 מֶ֣לֶךְ (oshb:Ps.29.10) are the noun, not the verb - so an unlabelled skeleton count of this clause overcounts by 2 verses.

challenges.claim: Quote and gloss do not cover the same span at web:Ps.96.13: a whole-verse Hebrew run is paired with an English quote of the verse's closing 2 cola only.
challenges.evidence: The rationale pairs “He will judge the world with righteousness, the peoples with his truth.” (web:Ps.96.13) with a byte run covering all 13 words of oshb:Ps.96.13. The English quote renders יִשְׁפֹּֽט תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בֶּאֱמוּנָתֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.96.13) only; the opening לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָ֨ה כִּ֬י בָ֗א כִּ֥י בָא֮ לִשְׁפֹּ֪ט הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ (oshb:Ps.96.13) has no counterpart in the quote, and WEB carries it as “before Yahweh; for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth.” (web:Ps.96.13). This is expansion-without-recut: either the English quote widens to the full verse or the Hebrew run cuts to the 5 words it glosses.

reviews.reasoning: The span Ps.97.1-Ps.97.6 is right and its opening is well warranted: יְהוָ֣ה מָ֭לָךְ תָּגֵ֣ל הָאָ֑רֶץ (oshb:Ps.97.1) collates at byte tier and the verse-initial kingship clause is a genuine tier-1 opener for an untitled identity psalm. The theophany interior tiles as described across MT 97:2-97:5, and MT 97:6 closes the movement; the row's rejected_alternative correctly refuses a cut at 97:4. All 3 curly WEB quotes check verbatim. The 2 filed defects are in the sweep's scope and in the form label the row and the Ps 97 second-half row share at the 97:6|97:7 seam - by seam-pair discipline that cure is one edit installed on both rows.

challenges.claim: The verse-initial sweep is scoped to a range that is not the row's span, and its digit is tier-dependent while the tier is left unnamed.
challenges.evidence: The signal reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'the same clause form as web:Ps.99.1 (sweep: 2 verses share this verse-initial form in this span)'. Against the row's declared span Ps.97.1-Ps.97.6 the count is 1 verse, since web:Ps.99.1 lies outside it; no other range is declared. Re-derived book-wide on the verse-initial position with the object named first (the clause יְהוָ֣ה מָ֭לָךְ, oshb:Ps.97.1) and the unit named: byte = 2 verses, MT 97:1 and MT 99:1; accent_stripped = 3 verses, adding MT 93:1 whose מָלָךְ֮ (oshb:Ps.93.1) differs from מָ֭לָךְ (oshb:Ps.97.1) in accent only; skeleton = 4 verses, adding MT 10:16 where the token is the noun. The delivered digit 2 is therefore right only at byte tier and only book-wide, and the row names neither.

challenges.claim: The rationale's warrant for the 97:6|97:7 seam misidentifies the form and the addressee of the verse that opens the next unit.
challenges.evidence: The rationale reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'The address shifts at web:Ps.97.7 from cosmic description to an imperative aimed at idol-worshippers'. MT 97:7 opens יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ (byte, oshb:Ps.97.7), a prefix-conjugation form: its initial consonant is the third-person prefix, and Hebrew forms no third-person imperative. The plural imperatives this cluster elsewhere quotes are all 5 prefixless - לְ֭כוּ (oshb:Ps.95.1), בֹּ֭אוּ (oshb:Ps.95.6), הָב֣וּ (oshb:Ps.96.7), הִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ (oshb:Ps.96.9), שִׂמְח֣וּ (oshb:Ps.97.12) - 5 comparanda against which the 97:7 form is not one. Both witnesses read it as third person: WEB has “Let all them be shamed who serve engraved images” (web:Ps.97.7). The verse's only true imperative is הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ ל֝וֹ (byte, oshb:Ps.97.7), and its addressee is כָּל אֱלֹהִֽים (oshb:Ps.97.7), not the idol-servers, who stay in the third person throughout. The seam at 97:6|97:7 survives on the topic and addressee shift; the form label does not, and the same wording must be recut on the Ps 97 second-half row, which repeats it.

reviews.reasoning: The span Ps.97.7-Ps.97.12 closes the psalm at MT 97:12 of 12 and its opening seam at 97:6|97:7 is a real discourse shift, so the row's parent and its outer edges are right; the quoted run יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ כָּל עֹ֬בְדֵי פֶ֗סֶל (oshb:Ps.97.7) collates at byte tier and all 5 WEB quotes are verbatim. The row's declared confidence of medium is honest, and I read the interior as genuinely contestable: the row rebuts a weak rival (97:9 alone) while conceding, in its own rationale, the stronger one it does not rebut. Two defects are filed: the shared form label at the opening seam, and the unaddressed rival seam at 97:9|97:10.

challenges.claim: The row's opening warrant and its rejected_alternative both call the 97:7 form an imperative aimed at idol-worshippers; it is a third-person prefix form and the verse's only imperative addresses someone else.
challenges.evidence: The rationale reads (straight-quoted row wording): 'The strophe opens with the imperative ... aimed at idol-worshippers', and rejected_alternative repeats 'the idol-shame imperative opened at 97:7'. MT 97:7 opens יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ (byte, oshb:Ps.97.7), whose initial consonant is the third-person prefix; Hebrew forms no third-person imperative, and the 5 plural imperatives quoted elsewhere in this cluster are prefixless - לְ֭כוּ (oshb:Ps.95.1), בֹּ֭אוּ (oshb:Ps.95.6), הָב֣וּ (oshb:Ps.96.7), הִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ (oshb:Ps.96.9), שִׂמְח֣וּ (oshb:Ps.97.12). Both witnesses read third person: WEB “Let all them be shamed who serve engraved images” (web:Ps.97.7). The verse's one imperative is הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ ל֝וֹ (byte, oshb:Ps.97.7), addressed to כָּל אֱלֹהִֽים (oshb:Ps.97.7). The staged extract stages 0 morphology fields, so this is argued from the pointed bytes and both renderings; the seam itself is unaffected, and the cure is one edit installed on this row and on the Ps 97 opening row, which carries the same wording.

challenges.claim: A tier-1 rival seam at 97:9|97:10 goes unaddressed while rejected_alternative rebuts a weaker rival at 97:9.
challenges.evidence: MT 97:10 opens with a vocative plus a plural imperative, אֹהֲבֵ֥י יְהוָ֗ה שִׂנְא֫וּ (byte, oshb:Ps.97.10) - a new addressee and a new command, which WEB renders “You who love Yahweh, hate evil!” (web:Ps.97.10). That is exactly the signal pair this cluster treats as a strophe opener 2 rows earlier, where הָב֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת עַמִּ֑ים (oshb:Ps.96.7) - imperative plus vocative addressee - is made the seam at 96:6|96:7, and at 95:6 where בֹּ֭אוּ (oshb:Ps.95.6) opens a row. The rationale itself concedes the shift ('The address turns back to the congregation at web:Ps.97.10 with a fresh imperative'), yet rejected_alternative disposes only of a 97:9 row. On the criterion the row applies elsewhere, 97:7-97:9 (idol-servers shamed, Zion's response, direct address to Yahweh) and 97:10-97:12 (congregation addressed, closing with the imperative שִׂמְח֣וּ at oshb:Ps.97.12) are 2 coherent strophes. I do not assert the 6-verse row is wrong, but the stronger rival must be rebutted rather than the weaker one, and confidence should follow that rebuttal.
